findings.issue: Citation, number, session and source-tag check against the own-date feed and card. Every cited headline supports its sentence (direction, outlet and company role). Card values match instrument, session and horizon (1/5/20), curve wording matches the card (bear flattening, +41 bps, 10Y -6 bps over 5 obs), there is no numeric spot-FX, and the FB, SQ and Mercedes-Benz naming is period-correct. scope_limits: Reviewed only the own-date feed (2022-02-24 headlines, titles, srcs, stamps, cats), own-date card, BRIEF.md, the writer note and exclusions. Headlines are not article bodies. Day-granular 08:00 stamps cannot show intra-day timing. Stale-by-meaning for the Tesla recalls rests on headline wording only. n1278 (separatists' request, 23 Feb) and n1281 (Ukraine state of emergency) are kept as pre-cutoff events in line with the task's list of known items. No other date's material and no web access were used.

recommended_exclusions.reason: CNBC 'South Korea's central bank holds interest rates steady': the Bank of Korea decision is on 24 Feb local time, after the 00:00 UTC cutoff, despite the 23 Feb stamp.
Reuters 'Expert views on Russian forces invading Ukraine' (23 Feb stamp): its vintage relative to the invasion cannot be established, so it could carry post-cutoff content.

Reuters 'Nestle says operations running normally in Ukraine, continuity plans in place' (23 Feb stamp): this is the kind of statement issued on or after the invasion morning, so its time cannot be shown to be before cutoff.
Reuters 'China says Taiwan is not Ukraine as island raises alert level' (23 Feb stamp): the timing of the alert-level change relative to the cutoff is uncertain.
FT 'ETF investors pile into Russian equities and defence stocks' (23 Feb stamp): not shown to describe pre-invasion flows; removed from the draft.
